$comment: Routes that answer without a signed-in caller, on purpose. Read by the launch-readiness check
C1-ROUTE-AUTHZ, which matches each entry as "<METHOD> <route path>".
Every entry in publicRoutes must have a reason in publicRouteReasons saying what protects the route.
Declared by the owner on 2026-11-22 (planner question d1c10394): "Declare all six public, with the tightenings".

publicRouteReasons.GET /api/catalog/webhooks/github: A fixed answer that the GitHub webhook is deployed: it reads nothing and names no setting, and the POST beside it checks GitHub's signature.
publicRouteReasons.GET /api/catalog/webhooks/vercel-deploy: A fixed answer that the Vercel webhook is deployed: it reads nothing and names no setting, and the POST beside it checks Vercel's signature.
publicRouteReasons.GET /api/health: Uptime check that answers ok or error and the time, nothing else, limited to 60 requests a minute per address.
publicRouteReasons.GET /api/invitations/[token]: The handler asks for no sign-in, so an invited person can read their invitation: the 192-bit random token in the link is the key (stored as a hash, it expires and can be revoked), and lookups are limited to 30 a minute per address.
publicRouteReasons.POST /api/oauth/register: Open client registration for MCP connectors (RFC 7591), limited to 10 an hour per address with checked redirect addresses; a registered client gets nothing until a signed-in person approves it.
publicRouteReasons.POST /api/oauth/token: Code exchange for MCP connectors: it needs a single-use code, the exact redirect address and the PKCE verifier, and is limited to 30 requests a minute per address.
